questions.q: Why does this report use Import mode instead of DirectQuery?
options: The dataset is small and only needs a glance before a Monday call, so Import's faster visuals and offline editing outweigh DirectQuery's live-refresh benefit
DirectQuery is not supported for SQL Server data sources
Import mode is required whenever a native SQL query is used
DirectQuery cannot run aggregated queries
questions.explain: Import suits a small, infrequently-refreshed dataset like this one; DirectQuery's main advantage (live data) isn't needed for a glance-before-Monday report.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect Power BI to the data, rather than importing the raw tables directly?
options: By pasting the Lesson 3 T-SQL query into the SQL Server connector's Advanced options as a native query
By manually recreating the joins and GROUP BY using only Power Query's UI, with no SQL at all
By exporting the query results to a CSV file and importing that
By connecting to Production.Product only and ignoring the other three tables
questions.explain: Using Get Data > SQL Server > Advanced options > SQL statement lets Power BI run the exact Lesson 3 query and import its already-shaped result.

questions.q: Why is it better to run the GROUP BY and filtering in T-SQL rather than in Power Query here?
options: It keeps the heavy lifting on the database server and keeps the Power Query step simple, working with a small, already-shaped table
Power Query cannot perform any kind of grouping or aggregation
SQL Server requires all filtering to happen before Power BI connects
DAX measures cannot be written against ungrouped data
questions.explain: Pushing the join and aggregation into the source query means Power BI only has to import a small, clean result set rather than raw, ungrouped rows.

questions.q: What data type should TotalSalesAmount be checked for in Power Query, and why does this check matter?
options: Decimal Number (or Fixed Decimal Number) — SQL Server's money/numeric types can sometimes import as text, which would silently break later DAX measures
Whole Number — decimals are not supported in Power BI visuals
Date/Time — because it's derived from OrderDate
Text — so it can be used as a slicer later
questions.explain: Confirming the numeric type here, rather than discovering a text-typed column once DAX measures fail or return blank, is one of the three housekeeping checks the lesson recommends.

questions.q: What does an unexpectedly large row count after loading the query most likely indicate?
options: A problem with the GROUP BY or a join condition in the query
That Import mode was chosen instead of DirectQuery
That the query column names need to be renamed
That the report needs an additional slicer
questions.explain: With only a handful of territories and product lines, the row count should be small; a count far larger than expected points to a grouping or join issue, not a Power BI setting.
